surface_mechanism_description: The growth mechanism involves the chemisorption of trimethylaluminum (TMA) on hydroxyl surface groups, forming adsorbed (-O-)nAl(CH3)3-n with methane as a byproduct. Subsequent water exposure oxidizes the aluminum, recreating hydroxyl groups and forming additional methane.
evidence: Cellulose fibers (C6H10O5)n are the primary constituent in natural cotton, and the cellulose polymer presents a large number of -OH groups on the surface to react with the TMA. The growth mechanism is based on the chemisorption of Al(CH3)3 on -OH surface groups. This reaction forms adsorbed (-O-)nAl(CH3)3-n with CH4 as a byproduct. The H2O then recreates -OH surface groups by oxidation of the Al while also forming CH4.
